results.question: What are the rules for claiming per-diem allowances?
results.answer:
Employees travelling on approved business may claim daily meal and incidental allowances according to the following destination tiers:
- Tier 1 cities, including London, New York, Singapore, and Tokyo, carry a maximum per-diem of USD 85 per day.
- Tier 2 cities, including Dubai, Mumbai, Rotterdam, and Hamburg, carry a maximum per-diem of USD 65 per day.
- Tier 3 cities and other approved destinations carry a maximum per-diem of USD 45 per day. Per-diem allowances cover meals and reasonable incidental expenses. They do not cover hotel accommodation, airfare, or business entertainment.

results.question: How does the Travel & Expense Policy handle the combination of business travel with personal leave, and what additional responsibilities do employees have in such cases?
results.answer: The Travel & Expense Policy allows employees to combine approved business travel with personal leave where operational requirements permit. When business travel is combined with personal leave, the company will pay only the expenses directly attributable to the approved business portion. Additional personal accommodation, meals, transport, and travel changes must be paid by the employee. Employees must obtain written approval from their Line Manager and HR before combining business travel with personal leave. See Section 8.3 of the Leave Policy for the related leave-record requirements.

results.question: What is the process for requesting annual leave if an employee is not a full-time member of the team?
results.answer: The process for requesting annual leave is the same for all shore-based employees, regardless of their full-time status. Eligible full-time employees receive 24 working days of paid annual leave for each completed calendar year. Employees joining during the calendar year receive annual leave on a prorated basis, calculated at 2 working days for each completed month of service. Annual leave should be requested at least 7 calendar days before the intended start date. Requests involving more than 10 consecutive working days should be submitted at least 21 calendar days in advance. Any unused annual leave can be carried forward a maximum of 5 days into the following calendar year, provided it is used by 31 March. Any remaining balance after this date will normally expire.
